name: H5 Data Centers

profile.reading: Per H5 Data Centers own site, this Cleveland, Ohio facility sits at 1625 Rockwell Ave and totals 351,000 square feet, built to Tier III colocation standard with 2N UPS power and 2N backup generators rated for 48 hour diesel runtime. The page does not state a power capacity in MW. The facility offers access to 23 on-net carriers and the CL-IX, FD-IX, and Ohio IX internet exchanges, and is SOC 2, ISO 27001, and PCI-DSS compliant, with a 100 percent sales and use tax abatement under an Ohio incentive program. H5 Data Centers is a privately held US colocation and wholesale data center operator with facilities spanning roughly two dozen markets nationwide, per the company's own site, of which this Cleveland facility is one of its largest publicized builds at 351,000 square feet. Cleveland has drawn colocation and enterprise IT investment in part on the strength of Ohio's state and local data center tax abatement program, which the operator's own page cites directly, offering a 100 percent sales and use tax exemption on qualifying equipment purchases tied to job and investment commitments; this incentive has also drawn hyperscale investment elsewhere in the state, though that broader trend is not attributed to this specific building. H5 markets this facility for its access to 23 on-net carriers and three regional internet exchanges (CL-IX, FD-IX, and Ohio IX), positioning it as a Midwest interconnection point distinct from the coastal markets where H5 also operates. H5 is not a publicly traded company and does not file SEC disclosures, so this entry's power, cooling, and certification details are sourced solely to the operator's own published facility page rather than an independently corroborating source, a limitation this registry notes rather than treats as disqualifying, consistent with its general practice for privately held colocation operators. No year-opened date or third-party audited MW capacity figure was located for this specific address this session.
